paper_metadata.title: Multi-Task Identification of Entities, Relations, and Coreference for Scientific Knowledge Graph Construction
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2018)
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper introduces SciERC, a dataset with entity, relation, and coreference annotations for scientific articles, and SciIE, a unified multi-task framework with shared span representations. It argues that joint prediction reduces cascading errors, uses coreference to support cross-sentence information, outperforms prior scientific information-extraction models without domain-specific features, and supports scientific knowledge-graph construction.

paper_metadata-abstract-04-01.excerpt: We introduce a multi-task setup of identifying and classifying entities, relations, and coreference clusters in scientific articles... Experiments show that our multi-task model outperforms previous models in scientific information extraction without using any domain-specific features.

problem_addressed-05-01.excerpt: Organizing scientific information into structured knowledge bases requires information extraction (IE) about scientific entities and their relationships.

problem_addressed-05-02.excerpt: Most relation extraction systems are designed for within-sentence relations. However, extracting information from scientific articles requires extracting relations across sentences.

problem_addressed-05-03.excerpt: Our unified model is a multi-task setup that shares parameters across low-level tasks, making predictions by leveraging context across the document through coreference links.

methodology-primary_family-06-01.excerpt: We develop a unified learning model for extracting scientific entities, relations, and coreference resolution... avoiding cascading errors between tasks by jointly modeling all spans and span-span relations.

methodology-primary_family-06-02.excerpt: All three tasks of entity recognition, relation extraction, and coreference resolution are treated as multinomial classification problems with shared span representations.

methodology-secondary_families-07-01.excerpt: We use feedforward neural networks (FFNNs) over shared span representations g to compute a set of span and pairwise span scores.

methodology-secondary_families-07-02.excerpt: We first apply the SciIE model over single documents and then integrate the entities and relations across multiple documents.

problem_addressed: Scientific literature needs to be organized into structured knowledge bases, but scientific entity/relation extraction is costly and existing information-extraction pipelines suffer cascading errors and primarily model within-sentence relations. The objective is to jointly identify scientific entities, typed relations, and coreference clusters so cross-sentence relations can contribute to a denser scientific knowledge graph.

methodology.description: SciIE enumerates candidate within-sentence spans up to a maximum width, encodes the document with a one-layer BiLSTM, and constructs each span vector from its endpoint representations, attention-based soft headword, and span-width embedding. Task-specific FFNNs score entity labels, relation mentions, coreference mentions, relation pairs, and coreference pairs while sharing span representations. It jointly optimizes weighted entity, relation, and marginalized coreference losses. Beam pruning retains relation and coreference candidate spans, then the model outputs entity types, within-sentence typed relations, and antecedent links. For graph construction, it processes each abstract, uses coreference clusters to replace generic mentions and selects the longest cluster string, normalizes acronyms/plurals, retains frequent entities as nodes, merges substring variants, and assigns each entity-pair edge its most frequent relation type across the corpus.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: Uses a fixed task schema rather than an external ontology: six entity categories (Task, Method, Metric, Material, Other-ScientificTerm, Generic) and seven typed relations (Compare, Part-of, Conjunction, Evaluate-for, Feature-of, Used-for, Hyponym-Of). These types define graph node/edge semantics.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured natural-language scientific article abstracts (AI conference/workshop proceedings); the model input is a document represented as a sequence of words.
input_output.input_granularity: Document-level abstracts; candidate entities and relations are spans and within-sentence span pairs, while coreference links connect mentions across sentences.
input_output.output_representation: Typed entity spans, typed within-sentence relations, and coreference clusters; aggregated as a scientific knowledge graph whose nodes are normalized scientific entities and whose directed/symmetric typed edges are the most frequent extracted relations between entity pairs.

models_and_tools: Scientific Information Extractor (SciIE) unified multi-task model
Task-specific two-hidden-layer FFNN scorers with shared span representations
Attention-based soft-headword span representation and span-width embeddings
Beam pruning for relation and coreference candidate spans
Acronym expansion and plural-to-singular normalization heuristics for graph construction
datasets: SciERC: 500 annotated scientific abstracts from 12 AI conference/workshop proceedings; 8,089 entities, 4,716 relations, 2,752 coreference links, and 1,023 coreference clusters
Semantic Scholar Corpus: 110,000 AI-conference abstracts used to construct and analyze the knowledge graph

metrics: Precision, recall, and F1 for entity recognition and relation extraction
Average precision/recall/F1 across MUC, B3, and CEAFφ4 for coreference resolution
Precision versus pseudo-recall curves and AUC for human evaluation of the constructed knowledge graph
Cohen's kappa agreement for a subset of dataset annotations
baselines: E2E Coref (Lee et al., 2017) combined with ELMo
Luan et al. (2017b) semi-supervised neural keyphrase-extraction model
evaluation.setting: SciIE is evaluated on development and test sets for SciERC entity recognition, relation extraction, and coreference resolution, and on SemEval 2017 Task 10 for span identification, keyphrase extraction, relation extraction, and overall score. An ablation compares single-task training with adding the other task losses. For graph quality, four domain experts annotate relation triples involving ten randomly selected frequent entities (about 1,500 triples) and compare graphs built with versus without coreference links; recall is approximated by pseudo-recall because complete recall is infeasible.

value: On SciERC test, SciIE attained entity P/R/F1 of 67.2/61.5/64.2, relation P/R/F1 of 47.6/33.5/39.3, and coreference P/R/F1 of 52.0/44.9/48.2; the coreference score is the average of MUC, B3, and CEAFφ4.
On SciERC development, SciIE achieved entity F1 68.1, relation F1 39.5, and coreference F1 58.0; these exceeded the displayed baselines for each task.

The ablation on SciERC development found multi-task F1 68.1/39.5/58.0 for entity/relation/coreference versus single-task 65.7/37.9/55.3; adding coreference to relation extraction raised relation F1 from 37.9 to 39.5.

On SemEval 2017 Task 10, SciIE scored F1 58.6 for span identification, 46.0 for keyphrase extraction, 27.8 for relation extraction, and 44.7 overall; the displayed best SemEval scores were 55, 44, 28, and 43, respectively.
In graph human evaluation, the graph using coreference had AUC 0.751 versus 0.695 without coreference; both variants had precision above 84%, while the coreference variant had higher pseudo-recall.

value: Experimental finding: joint shared-span training improved all three SciERC tasks over the single-task ablation and the listed baselines.
Experimental finding: coreference-aware graph construction improved human-evaluation AUC (0.751 versus 0.695) and pseudo-recall while both graph variants retained precision above 84%.

Review-level inference: jointly modeling coreference with entity/relation extraction is particularly useful for document-level scientific Text-to-KG because it converts otherwise generic cross-sentence mentions into normalized graph entities.

Review-level inference: exhaustive span enumeration enables overlapping scientific spans and avoids the fixed BIO-tagging boundary constraint, which is consistent with the stronger SemEval span-identification result.

value: Author-stated limitation: there remains a large gap between model and human performance on scientific information extraction.
Author-stated limitation: the SemEval 2017 relation-extraction gain is smaller because that dataset lacks coreference links and has less comprehensive relation types.

Review-level inference: relation extraction remains the weakest of the three evaluated SciERC components by test F1 (39.3), so downstream graph edges are likely more error-prone than entity spans or coreference links.

Review-level inference: graph entity consolidation relies on surface-form heuristics (acronym replacement, singularization, longest cluster string, frequency and substring merging), rather than learned or ontology-based entity linking; this may not resolve semantic aliases not captured by those heuristics.
